options.text: Docker's modern, default build engine with parallel stages, smarter caching, and features like cache mounts

questions.explanation: BuildKit is the modern build engine, and it is the default in current Docker. It builds stages in parallel, caches more granularly, and supports mounts and build secrets.

questions.prompt: What does adding `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` as the first line do?

options.text: It tells BuildKit to use the current Dockerfile frontend, enabling modern features like RUN --mount
It runs the container as non-root

questions.explanation: The syntax directive selects the current stable Dockerfile frontend, unlocking features such as cache mounts and build secrets regardless of Docker version.

options.text: Because build and deploy machines can differ in CPU architecture (e.g. arm64 vs amd64), and one multi-platform image runs on each

questions.explanation: A single-architecture image will not run on a different architecture without emulation. A multi-platform image (a manifest list) provides the right build for each machine.

questions.prompt: The extended build command that manages builders and produces multi-platform images is docker ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: docker buildx, built on BuildKit, manages builders and can produce multi-platform images with --platform.

questions.prompt: Why does a multi-platform buildx build usually require --push rather than loading locally?

options.text: Because the local image store holds a single architecture, so the multi-platform manifest list is pushed to a registry instead
Because buildx cannot build locally at all

questions.explanation: The local store is single-architecture, so a multi-platform result cannot be loaded into it; you push the manifest list to a registry (or use --load for a single platform).

questions.prompt: What does a cache mount (RUN --mount=type=cache) do?

options.text: It bakes the package cache into the image as a layer
It persists a package manager's cache across builds without adding it to the image
It scans the image for vulnerabilities

questions.explanation: A cache mount keeps a download cache (pip, npm, apk) available across builds for speed, while keeping it out of the final image layers.
